problem: Bluetooth headset muffled/underwater in-game audio or no teammate voice after voice-chat patch (Hands-Free profile switch)
symptoms: Audio sounds muffled/mono/underwater only in match when voice chat is enabled
Cannot hear teammates (VC icons light up but no sound) or game audio vanishes
Menu/lobby audio normal
Bluetooth devices (AirPods, Sony XM4, Razer Kraken, Pixel Buds) affected
root_causes: Valorant update made Windows switch Bluetooth headset to Hands-Free/HFP telephony profile (low-bandwidth mono) when voice chat opens, even if headset mic is not the selected input
Riot support acknowledged as their bug, no ETA

fixes.fix: Disable 'Handsfree Telephony' service on the headset: Settings > Bluetooth & devices > More devices and printer settings > right-click headset > Properties > Services tab > untick Handsfree Telephony > Apply; disconnect/reconnect headset. Some guides: repeat while Valorant + voice chat running, then power-cycle headset. Costs the headset mic; setting may need repeating after restart
Disable Windows service 'Bluetooth Audio Gateway Service' (BTAGService) in services.msc (startup Disabled + Stop), restart PC
Turn off team/party voice chat in Valorant audio settings (temporary workaround)

Route audio through a virtual audio device/mixer so Valorant does not talk to the BT device directly: Voicemeeter Banana/Potato, VB-Cable, EarTrumpet, OBS monitoring, or NVIDIA Broadcast (mic+speaker optimization, select Broadcast devices in-game)
Use a separate non-Bluetooth microphone, select specific devices in Valorant instead of 'Default', disable other mics in Windows sound settings
Use a wired headset
Roll back Windows 11 to Windows 10 (one OP said this fixed it)
Switch headset app from ANC to normal and turn off hands-free telephony

diagnostic_signals: Bluetooth audio device present with Hands-Free Telephony / Handsfree service enabled
Default recording device is a Bluetooth headset mic
Sound control panel: BT device exposing both 'Headphones' and 'Headset' endpoints

problem: Discord stream: friends cannot hear Valorant voice chat while screen sharing
symptoms: Streamer's Discord viewers hear game sound but not teammates' voice chat after patch
root_causes: Valorant update change; Discord audio capture interaction

fixes.fix: Capture via OBS with a separate 'Game' output device added as audio source
Run Discord as admin (OP reported not working)
Discord Settings > Voice & Video > disable 'use an experimental method to capture audio from applications'

diagnostic_signals: Discord running, experimental audio capture setting

problem: Audio crackling when another audio source plays (USB audio interface)
symptoms: Crackling in Valorant only while Discord/Spotify plays, Scarlett 2i2 interface
root_causes: Outdated BIOS suspected

fixes.fix: Update motherboard BIOS

problem: PC reboots instantly (no BSOD) or BSODs with vgk.sys when launching Valorant - outdated motherboard BIOS
symptoms: Clicking Play makes PC black-screen and reboot within seconds
BSOD stop codes SYSTEM_SERVICE_EXCEPTION / SECURE_PCICONFIG_SPACE_ACCESS_VIOLATION (0x1EA) naming vgk.sys; VGS.sys on League
Uninstalling Vanguard may also BSOD
Reinstalls, DDU, SFC/DISM, Windows reset did not help
Started mid Dec 2025 patch; BIOS from 2019 typical
root_causes: Riot patch blocks/destabilises Vanguard on old BIOS/firmware (anti-injection protection); Vanguard needs a recent BIOS

fixes.fix: Update motherboard BIOS to latest from manufacturer (flash drive/EZ Flash etc.), back up/disable BitLocker first; afterwards re-enable Secure Boot, TPM/fTPM, UEFI (not CSM) because BIOS update resets them
After BIOS update also run sfc /scannow, DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth, DDU GPU driver reinstall, reinstall Vanguard
One poster also set msconfig boot processors to 12 cores after BIOS update
Safe mode removal of Vanguard then reinstall (temporary only, relapsed)
Full Windows wipe/reset (temporary, relapsed)
Failed BIOS flash can stick on logo; clear CMOS by pins

diagnostic_signals: BIOS version/date age (older than ~2023/2024) via Win32_BIOS / msinfo32
Minidump / event log BugCheck naming vgk.sys
Secure Boot/TPM status after BIOS update

problem: PC restarts on Valorant launch caused by external USB CD/Blu-ray drive
symptoms: Valorant launch restarts PC while external USB-C CD/DVD drive connected
root_causes: Peripheral conflicting with Vanguard

fixes.fix: Unplug external Blu-ray/CD drive

diagnostic_signals: Connected USB optical drive / unusual USB storage devices

problem: Vanguard requires Memory Integrity (HVCI) / Core Isolation enabled - VAN RESTRICTION or VAN 57 / won't launch
symptoms: Popup 'does not meet requirements: UEFI Secure Boot enabled, HVCI enabled'
Game fails to start or PC restarts at launch; 'Valorant corrupted' after enabling
Memory Integrity toggle shows incompatible/conflicting drivers or greyed out
BSOD gdrv3.sys when enabling HVCI
root_causes: Riot Vanguard restriction pushed to some accounts/devices (often Win10 or older systems) requiring HVCI; incompatible kernel drivers (gdrv3.sys Gigabyte, Realtek audio driver) block Memory Integrity
Restriction may be tied to account and last ~30 days

fixes.fix: Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation > turn on Memory Integrity; reboot; Valorant 'repair' if it reports corrupted files
Remove/update incompatible driver blocking Memory Integrity: boot safe mode and delete gdrv3.sys (Gigabyte) / update or reinstall Realtek audio driver, then enable Memory Integrity
Enable Secure Boot + virtualization (SVM/VT-x) in BIOS before HVCI will stay on
Wait out restriction (~30 days) if HVCI cannot be enabled; Riot says no exception

diagnostic_signals: Drivers incompatible with HVCI (gdrv3.sys, old Realtek audio)

problem: VAN 9003 / 'UEFI Secure Boot verification failure' (VAN RESTRICTION 1) although Secure Boot looks enabled in BIOS
symptoms: Vanguard says Secure Boot must be enabled but BIOS shows enabled / 'Not Active'
msinfo32 Secure Boot State = Off
Windows Boot Manager blocked by security policy after enabling Secure Boot (Lenovo LOQ)
Secure Boot option greyed out
root_causes: Secure Boot keys missing/corrupt or platform in Setup mode, CSM enabled, BIOS update or crash resets defaults
Lenovo LOQ BIOS LZCN43WW Secure Boot bug

fixes.fix: In BIOS Secure Boot > Key Management: 'Install default/factory keys' or 'Reset to factory keys', then verify msinfo32 Secure Boot State = On
Reset BIOS to factory defaults and remove CMOS battery a few minutes (unplug PC first)
Disable CSM / set UEFI boot mode so Secure Boot option becomes available (disk must be GPT)
Lenovo LOQ: flash older BIOS (lzcn39ww then lzcn38ww via Back Flash) then enable Secure Boot
Follow a YouTube video for enabling Secure Boot on ASUS TUF (worked for OP)
Convert MBR to GPT so UEFI can be used

diagnostic_signals: msinfo32 Secure Boot State and BIOS Mode (UEFI vs Legacy)
Disk partition style GPT vs MBR (Get-Disk)

problem: TPM 2.0 requirement on old PCs / Windows 10 vs Windows 11
symptoms: Vanguard asks for TPM 2.0 on old hardware
Disabling TPM stops stutter but game crashes with VAN00098
root_causes: TPM 2.0 required on Windows 11 (Win10 not required unless flagged); installing Win11 via TPM bypass triggers Vanguard TPM demand

fixes.fix: On Windows 10 disable VBS (virtualization-based security) if it blocks; enable TPM/fTPM in BIOS
Windows 10 without TPM 2.0 can still play unless account is flagged; no workaround on Win11 without TPM

problem: VAN RESTRICTION on device/account that cannot be removed
symptoms: Support says restriction is system-managed and cannot be lifted; HWID ban claims on new laptop
root_causes: Automated device restriction / HWID ban

fixes.fix: Wait until restriction expires; submit support tickets with proof (no confirmed removal)

problem: VAN 185 - Vanguard connection lost / kicked mid-match
symptoms: Kicked from game after 5-7 minutes or randomly; vgc service stops
Recurs after updates
Voice chat cut before kick
root_causes: Conflicting third-party software (Overwolf installed unknowingly)
Unstable connection/ISP routing to Riot servers
Network drivers/cable faults, controller plugged in, vgc service set Manual

fixes.fix: Uninstall Overwolf (and other overlay/injection apps)
Network reset (Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset); ipconfig flushdns; disable IPv6; public DNS
services.msc: set vgc to Automatic
Unplug game controller, swap Ethernet/Wi-Fi, replace cable, VPN (Cloudflare)
Clean Vanguard reinstall (Revo), delete %localappdata%\VALORANT\saved config, log out of all devices
Check Device Manager for yellow-exclamation drivers
Restart modem / try hotspot / ISP routing issue

problem: Stutter / micro-freezes every few seconds only in Valorant - Realtek 2.5GbE (inactive NIC) driver/interrupts
symptoms: Frame drops from hundreds of fps to single digits every ~1-60 seconds
Only Valorant affected on high-end new PCs (9800X3D, 5070, 7600X, 9600X)
Sometimes persists after closing game; lag in menu/chat
root_causes: Realtek 2.5GbE / unused network adapter driver generating DPC/interrupt latency (old Windows-supplied driver, 2021); conflicts with Vanguard

fixes.fix: Device Manager > Network adapters: disable the adapter you do not use (Realtek 2.5GbE Ethernet when on Wi-Fi, or Wi-Fi when on Ethernet; also unused Bluetooth); update Realtek driver from motherboard maker or run Realtek NDIS config tool
Work through r/AMDHelp optimization guide steps 5, 9, 12 (and 1-7,10,11) - OP reported 5,9,12 fixed it
Disable x3D turbo mode, set global C-states Enabled in BIOS (X3D CPUs); disable HAGS and Game Mode
Disable the NIC in BIOS

diagnostic_signals: Network adapters list: Realtek 2.5GbE present and driver date/version
Both Ethernet and Wi-Fi adapters active

problem: Valorant stutter or freeze caused by background software (overlays, wallpaper, trackers, tray apps)
symptoms: Stutter/freeze when opening chat, menu lag, black screen on Aero Peek, high memory use
root_causes: Wallpaper Engine (even paused / 'Unpause during Aero Peek')
Bluetooth tray app BTTray.exe
Valorant tracker overlays after UI update
Clipping/overlay apps (SteelSeries GG, Medal, Xbox Game Bar, Radeon)
Bonjour / National Instruments software

fixes.fix: Close Wallpaper Engine entirely / disable 'Unpause during Aero Peek'
Disable BTTray.exe in Task Manager startup apps
Close/uninstall Valorant tracker app
Uninstall Bonjour / National Instruments to fix 10% loading hang
Close redundant clipping/overlay apps

diagnostic_signals: Running processes: wallpaper engine, BTTray.exe, tracker apps, medal, steelseries, overwolf, bonjour service

problem: Valorant stutters/low 1% lows fixed by running OBS game capture in background
symptoms: 1% lows 11fps, feels 60Hz on 240Hz
root_causes: GPU clocks/power state not kept high or GameBar scheduling issue

fixes.fix: Run OBS with Game Capture in background; removed Xbox Game Bar
Balanced/best performance power plan

diagnostic_signals: GPU clock idle drops, power plan, Game Bar presence

problem: Stutter after fresh install / new GPU: live shader compilation
symptoms: Frame drops in new maps/agents after reinstall or GPU swap
root_causes: UE5 compiles shaders live

fixes.fix: Play range using all agents/abilities/guns and load maps; stutter fades

problem: Low FPS (3-5 fps) / capped FPS / stutter - GPU driver, AMD settings, page file
symptoms: Constant 3-5fps even in menu
FPS capped by AMD software/custom resolution
FPS drop after enabling SVM
root_causes: Latest GPU driver faulty; AMD panel profile limits; page file misconfig

fixes.fix: DDU uninstall display drivers, install slightly older WHQL driver (NVIDIA 591.44), clean install
AMD: reset game profile, delete custom resolutions, disable fps limiters/vsync, keep only Enhanced Sync; windowed mode + disable fullscreen optimizations
Page file: disable all, restart, set C: initial/max 16384 MB
DDU reinstall for freeze/black screen (problem later resolved by itself)

problem: Entire PC freezes in cycles after launching Valorant (new AMD builds, LiveKernelEvent 141, shutdown hangs)
symptoms: System freezes shortly after Valorant start, persists after closing, restart/shutdown hangs
LiveKernelEvent 141/144/15e
Black screen with monitor disconnect
root_causes: Realtek NIC driver (see Realtek problem)
Recent AMD chipset/GPU driver
Firewall interfering with Vanguard connection
USB selective suspend
iGPU disabled in BIOS
XMP misconfiguration
Secure Boot OS type wrong

fixes.fix: Disable Realtek ethernet/unused adapter (fixed LiveKernelEvent 141)
Whitelist Valorant, Riot Client, Vanguard in Windows Firewall/antivirus (Riot support)
Disable USB selective suspend; re-enable iGPU in BIOS
Roll back AMD GPU/chipset drivers via DDU
Update BIOS / check XMP; Secure Boot OS type Windows UEFI mode
DDU reinstall GPU driver

problem: Valorant won't start from desktop shortcut / loading screen loops - Riot Client tray state
symptoms: Click does nothing; loading icon disappears; Play loops
Works from Riot Client or tray
Cannot uninstall because Riot Client is running
root_causes: Riot Client hidden in system tray; corrupted install/shortcut
Third-party firewall + riot settings yaml; Vanguard not initialized

fixes.fix: Launch via Riot Client from system tray; right-click tray Riot Client > Exit before uninstalling
Uninstall everything (client, game, Riot Games folder, shortcuts), reboot to unload Vanguard, reinstall, new shortcut
Edit shortcut to run RiotClientServices.exe without --launch args
Delete third-party firewall and Riot Client settings yaml, run as admin
Reinstall Vanguard, repair, then set Memory Integrity on
Restart PC (Vanguard first-run restart)

problem: Riot Client update/install fails (update loop, 'Something went wrong', VAL 43 stuck at loading)
symptoms: Update button resets; install error; stuck load 10%
root_causes: Corrupt client, outdated installer 116.0.1.3585 served, Bonjour DLL conflicts, kernel-level corruption

fixes.fix: Riot client profile > Repair; or restart PC; or disable auto updates; or exit Vanguard in tray, reboot
Download installer via different browser/VPN to get newer build (123.02.3988+)
Uninstall Bonjour app (conflicts with Vanguard) for VAL 43
Windows in-place repair upgrade via Media Creation Tool keeping files/apps for VAL 43

root_causes: Corrupt Riot install; Wi-Fi repeater/ISP routing

Restart PC/close client then relaunch (ping stuck)
ipconfig /release /renew /flushdns, netsh winsock reset (temporary)
Cloudflare WARP made friends/chat service work (Service Unavailable) but ping 200ms; later resolved on its own
